text: This mountain is almost perfectly symmetric.
So why would a volcano that erupts about every 8 years stay so neat?
This is Mayan, in the Philippines, 2,462 meters tall, about 7 Eiffel Towers.
And on the 30th of October, it erupted again, firing ash 3 kilometers into the sky.
Here's the thing, most mountains get old, rain and wind carve them up.
But Maon never gives them time. It has erupted around 50 times since 1616,
and every time, fresh rock piles up around the top, layer on layer. I can't erode it fast enough.
So why is it so restless? Maon sits on the ring of fire. Here, one tectonic plate slides
under another, melts and feeds the volcano. So here's the twist. Maon isn't perfect
despite its eruptions, it's perfect because of them.
Even its name comes from Ma Gaon, a local word for beautiful.
Beauty takes work every few years.
